(AML/CFT obligations); French Commercial Code, Articles L123-7 and R123-220 to R123-233 (register of beneficial owners); Ordonnance n°2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 (transposition of AML Directive 2015/849); Décret n°2018-284 of 18 April 2018 (UBO register filing procedure); Law n°2017-1839 of 9 December 2017 (Sapin II) on transparency and anti-corruption.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each foreign individual shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner, including specimen signature page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's / director's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization through the French Embassy/Consulate if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and current certificate of good standing of each non-French corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry / Registrar of Companies in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or Consular Legalization at the French Embassy/Consulate if applicable, followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of each non-French shareholder approving the formation of the French SAS, the appointment of the SAS President, and the governance terms
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors / shareholders' meeting of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the French formation representative, counsel, and registered-office domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder(s) and authorized signatories of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the issuing jurisdiction; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered-agent certificate setting out the ownership chain, UBO identification, source of funds, and absence of PEP/sanction flags
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's registered agent, professional bank, or licensed compliance provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where required, otherwise recognized by French AML/CFT obliged entities through internal certification; certified French translation if used in French proceedings

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Regulations (EU) No 2580/2001 and 269/2014), UN Security Council sanctions as implemented in France, the French Treasury (DG Trésor) asset-freeze list, and the Bank of France/FICOV list of non-cooperative jurisdictions. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person (PEP), and OFAC screening is recommended because the target payment rails include TikTok Creator Payout and Wise B2B which may route through US financial institutions. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years under Article L561-12 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and Guichet Unique: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the official filing language. Corporate names may include foreign words but must be transliterated into Latin script, and any foreign-language name must be accompanied by a French translation in the bylaws and in any public filing. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered in the RNCS, must not be contrary to public policy or good morals, and must not infringe third-party trademark rights.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: There is no true statutory name reservation in France; the INPI availability certificate and RNCS conflict search are treated as a due-diligence clearance valid for 30 days. If the name is rejected during Guichet Unique pre-control or by the registry, the applicant may file a written recours gracieux with the INPI within one month of notification. If that is refused, an appeal may be brought before the competent tribunal administratif within two months on procedural grounds. Where the opposition is based on an earlier company name or trademark, the dispute is resolved before the Tribunal de Commerce (or Tribunal Judiciaire) in accordance with the rules of unfair competition and civil liability. The applicant may simultaneously amend the draft bylaws and refile using a new distinctive name variant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted only in the regulated form of commercial domiciliation by an approved domiciliation provider. A pure virtual mailbox without a French legal address and demonstrable operational substance is not acceptable. For a digital creator MCN agency, domiciliation is commercially defensible for the first two years, but thereafter, tax residence and commercial-substance expectations require tangible business premises or credible outsourced operational facilities in France.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first 36 months for a low-risk digital services entity. The likelihood rises to 50-70% if the registered office is a mass-domiciliation address without signage, or if the entity files VAT refunds, uses cross-border payouts, or exhibits inconsistent staffing and revenue indicators.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II, Title I (commercial companies) and Title II, Chapter VII (SAS), especially Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20; R.123-1 to R.123-31 and R.123-130 concerning RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, acting through INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic incorporation dossier filed through the Guichet Unique (successor to the M0 form), resulting in the issue of the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital is imposed for an SAS; the Articles of Association determine the issued capital. Cash contributions must be fully subscribed and deposited in a blocked bank account or with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations before registration. Funds are released only upon presentation of the Kbis. Where the Articles permit partial release, the unpaid balance must be called within five years. In-kind contributions are subject to a report from a commissaire aux apports unless the applicable de minimis exemption applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporation formalities of the Company having been completed, the First Board hereby ratifies the Articles of Association and adopts the registered office provisionally at [address]. (2) The Board confirms the subscription and full payment of all issued shares in accordance with the share register. (3) [Name] is appointed President and sole director, with all powers granted by the Articles, including bank signing and representation. (4) The President is authorized to complete all post-registration tax and social security filings, to sign agreements, and to open corporate bank accounts. (5) The corporate minutes book and share register are opened under the President's custody.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, sign and execute the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and, where real-property contributions are made, a notary; not filed with a government window at this stage.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language statuts identifying the SAS form, share capital, share classes, corporate object, registered office, duration, president powers, and dividend rights. Each shareholder signs every page and the final signature page. Where a shareholder is a legal entity, its legal representative proves authority. If assets are contributed in kind, a valuation report by a commissaire aux apports must be attached before filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts SAS)
Identity documents of all shareholders
Power of attorney if a representative signs on behalf of a shareholder
Certified copy of corporate authorizing resolution if a shareholder is a legal entity
Contribution-in-kind valuation report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise or correct the statuts before the capital deposit step; no governmental penalty is triggered at this preparatory stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked capital account and obtain capital deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed bank in France or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the projected company name, transfer the cash capital, and obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds and the block undertaking from the bank. The bank will release the funds only after the Kbis has been issued. For non-cash contributions, appoint a commissaire aux apports and attach the contribution report to the Articles.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association
Corporate name and purpose confirmation
Identity documents of the future legal representative
Beneficial owner declaration and source-of-funds details
Bank account opening form and KYC questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to additional anti-money-laundering or KYC queries from the bank, correct the account name, or select another French credit institution to obtain the blocking attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish incorporation notice in a legal announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the required legal announcement containing the company form, name, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, president, and RCS city. Submit the notice to the chosen authorized legal gazette and pay the publication fee. Obtain the attestation de parution for submission to the Guichet Unique.
required_dossiers: Company legal announcement text
Articles of Association abstract or summary
Name and address of registered office
Formation date and financial data required by law
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL refuses or queries the notice, correct the statement and republish within the legal publication period to preserve the availability of the company name and date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the electronic formation dossier with the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.service-public.fr), forwarded to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Guichet Unique or use an accredited service-provider account. Select the creation of a commercial company and the SAS legal form. Complete all company data, upload the statutory documents, and pay the applicable fees. The Guichet routes the dossier to the RCS registry, tax administration, social security authorities, and statistical office.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic company creation application
Signed Articles of Association
Capital deposit attestation or banker's block certificate
Capital contribution auditor report, if applicable
Proof of registered office (lease, free occupancy letter, or ownership title)
Identity document of the president and any general manager
Criminal record certificate or sworn declaration for the president/manager
Legal publication certificate (attestation de parution)
Declaration of no disqualification or incapacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS Greffe issues a query or proposed rejection, provide supplementary documents or amend inconsistencies within 15 days through the same Guichet Unique. If a final refusal is issued, correct the dossier and file a fresh application together with the applicable fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Kbis and verify post-registration data
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / INPI; successive automatic notifications to INSEE, DGFiP, and URSSAF.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the issued Extrait Kbis for exact legal identity, SIREN/SIRET numbers, NAF/APE code (mapping ISIC 7310 to NAF 73.11Z), registered office, legal form, and president's identity. The Kbis constitutes the official corporate identity extract and all commercial contracts must reference these details.
required_dossiers: Issued Kbis extract
SIREN/SIRET notification from INSEE
First board resolution and corporate books
Share register and register of share movements
Corporate minutes book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a request for rectification with the Guichet Unique or the Greffe if any Kbis field is inaccurate. No new incorporation fee is required for clerical corrections made within a reasonable period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate tax, social and governance arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), URSSAF, INSEE, and commercial insurers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the company is automatically registered for corporate income tax and value-added tax. Complete the employer registration if staff will be hired, subscribe to occupational health insurance, arrange office liability and property insurance, and hold the first formal board meeting to open bank accounts and approve governance procedures.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract and SIREN/SIRET registration
Corporate bank details and deposit certificate
Identity document of the president
Beneficial ownership declaration
Employment contract templates if hiring staff
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If automatic tax or social registrations are not received, contact DGFiP, URSSAF and the competent Centre de Formalités des Entreprises directly to complete the registrations without duplicative filings.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure digital creator MCN agency. If a physical production studio is later established, the competent authorities would be the Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the relevant municipal authorities for land-use and classified-installation permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific statutory operating license applies. The general eligibility to operate is evidenced by the Kbis extract under NAF/APE 73.11Z and, if a physical office is leased, by a standard commercial lease in compliance with the Code de commerce.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autorité environnementale relevant of the Ministère de la Transition Écologique, coordinated with DREAL where applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital service and advertising agency without industrial installation; no environmental impact assessment or ICPE registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. No process wastewater, volatile organic compound emissions, or regulated air pollutants are generated. Office and municipal waste must be disposed through authorised municipal waste collection channels under local waste-management by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must comply with the fire-safety and accessibility requirements of the Code de la construction et de l'habitation for établissements recevant du public where the premises are open to clients. The employer must prepare and maintain the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP), provide adequate emergency exits and fire extinguishers, and subscribe to mandatory workplace accident and employer liability insurance. Structural load clearance is not applicable because no industrial equipment is installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques, DGFiP), administered through the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Primary online infrastructure: impots.gouv.fr professional portal and the business formalities one-stop shop operated through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique. French VAT identification numbers are issued and administered by the DGFiP.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated and reported through the INPI Guichet unique, which transmits formation data to the commercial registry, INSEE and the DGFiP. The entity receives a SIREN number for the legal entity and a SIRET number for each establishment. The competent SIE assigns a French intra-Community VAT number, generally in the format FR plus a two-character control key and the nine-digit SIREN, after validating the entity and its taxable activities. The company must activate its professional account on impots.gouv.fr, register for corporate income tax and VAT obligations, identify the applicable VAT regime, and provide bank, registered-office, activity and beneficial-owner information where requested. A foreign entity without a French establishment must request French VAT registration from the competent SIE when it conducts French-taxable transactions requiring registration. An EU-established taxable person generally does not require a French fiscal representative; a non-EU-established taxable person carrying out French VAT-taxable transactions generally must appoint an accredited French tax representative, subject to applicable mutual-assistance exceptions. VAT registration does not by itself create a permanent establishment for corporate income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). A qualifying SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for a maximum of five financial years, if statutory conditions concerning age of the company, business activity, ownership, employee numbers and turnover or balance-sheet size are satisfied. The election is subject to prescribed timing and notification requirements and is not a general United States-style check-the-box election. France has no general entity-classification election permitting a SAS to select partnership treatment without satisfying the statutory IR option. Anti-hybrid-mismatch rules under the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance framework may deny deductions or require inclusion for arrangements producing deduction-without-inclusion or double-deduction outcomes; they do not constitute a routine entity election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT/TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no general VAT registration threshold for a business that is liable to French VAT outside the franchise regime. For French-established businesses eligible for the VAT franchise, the principal annual turnover thresholds are EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods, sales for consumption on premises and accommodation, and EUR 37,500 for services and non-commercial activities. Tolerance thresholds are generally EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively. Exceeding the applicable threshold can cause VAT liability from the statutory date and requires timely registration or regime change. Cross-border services, intra-Community acquisitions, imports, exports, and transactions subject to reverse charge can create registration, reporting or identification obligations independently of domestic turnover thresholds. For intra-Community distance sales and certain electronically supplied consumer services, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold and the One Stop Shop rules may apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting under the 2024 Finance Law timetable. From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices; large and intermediate-sized businesses must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from that date. Small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises must generally issue domestic B2B electronic invoices from 1 September 2027. Transactions with consumers and certain cross-border transactions are generally subject to electronic transaction reporting rather than domestic B2B invoice transmission. Invoices are transmitted through an approved private platform (plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire, PDP), with the public portal retaining directory and data-exchange functions under the implementation model. France does not operate a universal pre-clearance or real-time digital-stamping system for every invoice comparable to a mandatory continuous transaction control regime. Electronic invoices must contain required French VAT data, structured or hybrid machine-readable information, customer identification, VAT treatment, payment and transaction data, and must satisfy authenticity, integrity and legibility requirements. Sector-specific public-procurement e-invoicing rules may also apply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to a destination outside the European Union may be invoiced without French VAT when the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the exporter or qualifying intermediary can substantiate exit from the EU customs territory through accepted customs records. The exporter must retain a customs export declaration and evidence of actual exit, with the exporter of record and transaction chain correctly identified. Services supplied to a business customer established outside France are generally taxed according to the B2B place-of-supply rule and are outside the scope of French VAT in France rather than technically zero-rated, subject to customer-status and use-and-enjoyment rules. Services supplied to an EU business customer are generally subject to the reverse charge in the customer's Member State. Services supplied to consumers require separate place-of-supply analysis. A creator-MCN agency must distinguish agency services, advertising or marketing services, rights licensing, platform fees, digital services and creator payouts, because characterization and customer status can change the VAT treatment. Input VAT refunds require valid purchase invoices and a direct economic link to taxable transactions, including qualifying exports.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration containing the correct exporter, declarant, consignee, commodity, value and procedure data
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods left the European Union customs territory
Commercial invoice, transport documentation and packing or delivery records sufficient to reconcile the goods, parties and export transaction
Contract, purchase order and accounting records establishing the export sale and the applicable VAT treatment
Proof of customer identity and non-EU destination where relevant
Bank payment evidence may support commercial substantiation but is not a universal French statutory substitute for customs exit evidence
An inward remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory French export-VAT document and France has no universal requirement to collect export proceeds through a prescribed banking certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds and no universal 180-day repatriation rule for claiming export VAT treatment. The DGFiP may deny the VAT exemption or reverse a refund where export status, customer status, place of supply, customs exit, transaction reality or invoice data is not substantiated. Unpaid or improperly refunded VAT may be assessed retrospectively, together with late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month and tax penalties that may include 40% for deliberate failure and 80% for fraudulent activity or fraudulent manoeuvres, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Customs duties, import VAT, customs interest and customs penalties may apply separately where customs declarations or proof of exit are inaccurate. Serious intentional VAT fraud may also generate criminal exposure under French tax and criminal law. Records, invoices, contracts, platform settlement reports, creator payment schedules, customer-location evidence, customs data and banking records should be retained for the applicable French statutory audit and limitation periods.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the oversight of the European Central Bank; the French Treasury and the Directorate General of Customs and Indirect Taxes also administer relevant external-payment, statistical, and trade-reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange-control regime restricting ordinary current-account payments, including payment for services, royalties, imports, dividends, interest, and other legitimate commercial obligations. The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, customs, beneficial-ownership, and documentation requirements. A French SAS may generally receive foreign capital, retain foreign-currency balances, convert funds, and remit dividends or other distributions to non-resident shareholders after satisfaction of corporate-law, accounting, solvency, withholding-tax, transfer-pricing, and beneficial-ownership requirements. Dividend distributions require distributable profits and proper corporate approval; interim dividends require statutory conditions. Interest, royalties, management fees, and intra-group service payments must be commercially justified, arm's-length, properly documented, and reviewed for French withholding tax, treaty relief, VAT, and transfer-pricing consequences. Banks may delay, reject, or report transactions that lack a clear economic purpose or adequate source-of-funds evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a central bank and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export and cross-border service proceeds may generally be retained in euros or foreign currencies and held in France or abroad, subject to accounting, tax, customs, statistical, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Payment-service providers and banks may request invoices, contracts, proof of delivery or service performance, counterpart information, and transaction-purpose evidence. Large or unusual international payments may be subject to regulatory reporting or enhanced due diligence. Cash movements and certain payment transactions are subject to applicable European Union and French reporting rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; optional capital-deposit account for SAS share-capital formation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant regional Crédit Agricole caisse
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; optional capital-deposit account for SAS share-capital formation
Operational Account; optional capital-deposit account for SAS share-capital formation

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE group bank, including Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Épargne
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; optional capital-deposit account for SAS share-capital formation
Operational Account; optional capital-deposit account for SAS share-capital formation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for transactional payments and foreign-exchange operations, but not a complete substitute for a French relationship bank. A regulated European Union electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide payment accounts, safeguarding, SEPA payments, cards, and foreign-exchange services, subject to its licence, passporting status, product terms, and risk policy. Wise Europe SA is a Belgian authorised payment institution and its business service is not equivalent to a French bank deposit account; availability, local account details, inbound funds, safeguarding, payment limits, and supported currencies are product-specific. Offshore or non-European digital EMIs create higher onboarding, settlement, sanctions, and account-closure risk and may not provide a French IBAN or capital-deposit certificate. They should not be used as the sole rail for French share-capital formation, payroll, taxes, regulated client-money flows, or material TikTok platform receipts without written confirmation of account functionality and compliance acceptance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors appear physically at a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted after reliable identification and verification of the legal entity, directors, authorised signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, business model, source of funds, expected transactions, and tax residency. In practice, banks may require a video interview, certified corporate documents, a French address or operating nexus, an in-person appointment, or a local representative, particularly where the company is newly incorporated, foreign-owned, managed from abroad, or active in creator-platform payment flows. The bank determines the operational requirement under its risk-based procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder chain is incomplete, opaque, or includes nominee shareholders, trusts, bearer instruments, or jurisdictions viewed as high risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis extract or registration evidence; ownership chart to each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner; passports and residential-address evidence for owners, directors, and authorised signatories; shareholder register; corporate resolutions; and, where relevant, notarised or certified foreign corporate documents with translation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description is inconsistent with expected flows, particularly high-volume creator payouts, platform receipts, advertising payments, or payments to talent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business memorandum; platform agreements; creator and influencer agreements; agency commission model; sample invoices; expected monthly payment volumes and countries; counterpart categories; payment-flow diagram; projected cash-flow statement; and explanation of the distinction between company revenue, creator pass-through amounts, commissions, and reimbursable expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital, shareholder loans, or subsequent treasury funding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funding entity; dividend or retained-earnings evidence; shareholder-loan agreement; board approvals; capital contribution documentation; tax-residency evidence; proof of beneficial ownership of the funding account; and a clear payment reference identifying capital, share premium, or loan proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk countries, sanctioned persons, politically exposed persons, adverse media, or unexplained third-party payments appear in the ownership or payment chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and PEP screening records; adverse-media review; written explanation of counterpart relationships; enhanced due-diligence memorandum; contracts and invoices; proof of legitimate commercial purpose; compliance policies; and, where appropriate, independent legal or audit confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The company appears to hold creator funds, client money, or payment proceeds for onward transmission without an appropriate regulatory analysis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Funds-flow map; contractual allocation of payment obligations; evidence that the SAS acts as an agent or service provider rather than a payment institution; segregation and reconciliation procedures where contractually required; legal memorandum on payment-services perimeter; and confirmation that regulated payment services are supplied by an authorised provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax residency, management location, permanent-establishment exposure, or foreign operating nexus is unclear.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French registered-office evidence; lease or domiciliation agreement; director and employee location data; organisation chart; management and board-process description; tax-identification documents; certificates of tax residence where applicable; and an explanation of foreign branches, contractors, and platform accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected foreign-exchange activity is unsupported or inconsistent with the stated low-risk business profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Currency exposure schedule; customer and supplier currency matrix; treasury policy; forecast conversion volumes; hedging rationale; underlying contracts; invoice samples; and evidence that derivatives will be used for identifiable commercial exposures rather than speculative trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or inconsistent corporate records, expired identification documents, or unauthorised account-opening instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent Kbis extract; certified articles; registered-office evidence; beneficial-owner filing evidence; director appointment documents; powers of attorney; specimen signatures; current identification documents; and board or shareholder resolutions approving accounts, signatories, borrowing, and treasury authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity contributions and shareholder loans from an account held in the name of the identified shareholder or lender to the SAS corporate account through SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments or SWIFT cross-border transfer for non-euro payments. Use an unambiguous reference such as 'share capital contribution', 'share premium contribution', or 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]'; do not combine capital with unrelated operating receipts. For a newly formed SAS, obtain the bank or notary capital-deposit certificate, complete incorporation and registration, then release the funds to the operating account. Maintain the subscription decision, contribution agreement, source-of-funds evidence, bank confirmations, accounting entries, and beneficial-owner information. For foreign-currency transfers, retain the original currency amount, exchange-rate evidence, converted euro amount, fees, and reconciliation. The receiving bank may request the purpose, funding source, ownership chain, tax residence, and supporting agreements. Avoid third-party funding, cash deposits, payment splitting, or unexplained round-dollar transfers. Shareholder loans and related-party funding must be documented, booked, priced on an arm's-length basis, and reviewed for French interest-deduction, withholding-tax, thin-capitalisation, transfer-pricing, and hybrid-mismatch rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area, subject to bank limits and beneficiary validation. Use SWIFT MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent for non-SEPA or non-euro payments, with complete beneficiary, intermediary-bank, purpose, invoice, and sanctions-screening data. Use commercial documentary letters of credit, including SWIFT MT700 issuance and related amendment, presentation, and settlement messages, only where transaction value and counterparty risk justify documentary control. For ordinary creator, platform, advertising, software, and professional-service payments, standard bank transfer with contract and invoice support is generally more appropriate than a commercial LC. Maintain purchase orders or contracts, invoices, delivery or performance evidence, beneficiary tax and registration details, VAT treatment, withholding-tax analysis, and approval records. Screen beneficiaries, banks, countries, and vessels or goods where relevant. Do not route creator proceeds through personal accounts or make payments to unrelated third parties without a documented assignment or agency basis. Reconcile bank statements to the general ledger and creator-level sub-ledgers, and preserve payment and FX records for accounting, tax, audit, and AML purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorised bank or regulated investment firm, supported by documented forecast or committed commercial exposure and governed by an ISDA or equivalent treasury agreement where appropriate.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or unavailable, subject to counterparty eligibility, applicable local rules, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation requirements, and documented underlying exposure.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency-mismatch management, subject to bank documentation, collateral terms, accounting treatment, and exposure limits.
Currency options and zero-cost option structures for identified commercial exposures, subject to suitability, premium, termination, valuation, and governance controls.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps where required to hedge a documented currency and interest-rate exposure associated with qualifying financing.

Treasury policy controls requiring board-approved limits, authorised counterparties, segregation of dealing and settlement duties, confirmation matching, valuation, collateral monitoring, hedge-accounting assessment, and prohibition of speculative trading.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements deposit (Dépôt des comptes annuels) with the Commercial and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS registry of the registered office's court district)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the annual ordinary general meeting's approval of accounts; the AGM must itself be convened within six months of fiscal year-end (June 30 following a December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After 30 days of late filing the registry issues a formal notice (mise en demeure); civil fine up to EUR 7,500 for the legal entity and EUR 1,500 for directors; two consecutive omissions trigger judicial strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and loss of standing before public authorities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Liasse Fiscale, Form 2065-SD, annexes and intercompany/transfer-pricing documentation where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP - Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end: May 3 for paper filing and the third business day following May 1 for electronic filing (DGFIP calendar typically applies a mid-May online cut-off); for non-calendar fiscal year-ends, within three months of fiscal close
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; late-filing penalty of 10% of assessed corporate income tax, raised to 40% after formal notice; willful omission constitutes tax fraud punishable by up to EUR 500,000 fine and five years' imprisonment for the responsible director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and updating of the Beneficial Owner Declaration (Déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs / RBE register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (integrated with the RCS and cross-checked at the annual accounts deposit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration at incorporation; any shareholding change exceeding 25% of capital or voting rights, or any change of legal control, must be declared within 30 days; annual factual confirmation is submitted together with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal sanctions: up to six months' imprisonment and EUR 7,500 fine for individuals; up to EUR 37,500 fine for the legal entity for non-declaration or inaccurate declarations; the SAS may also be excluded from public procurement until the RBE is brought into conformity (Monetary and Financial Code Art. L561-2-1, L574-5).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary general meeting (AGO) approving the annual accounts, allocating profit or loss and recording decisions in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory records (Registre des décisions / minute book maintained at the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end unless the SAS articles of association provide otherwise within the statutory minimums; the commercial court may extend the period on a justified petition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic dissolution, but dividend distributions are invalid until accounts are approved; directors are exposed to civil liability for resulting corporate loss; the commercial court may oblige the president to convene the shareholders on request of any interested party or the public prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax declaration and settlement (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises - CFE, Form 1327-CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP, collected on behalf of local territorial authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration due by December 15 of each tax year (mandatory e-filing); instalment schedules apply to taxpayers above thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge plus 0.20% monthly interest; enforced recovery proceedings (avis de mise en recouvrement) may be commenced, and unpaid CFE may be publicly secured on the company's movable and immovable assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: RCS event-driven modification filings and register upkeep (registered office, president and officers, capital changes, by-law amendments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via the formalities guichet unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of each corporate event requiring registration against the RCS file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 1,500 per officer and up to EUR 7,500 for the legal entity; unregistered modifications are unopposable to third parties and may delay banking and MCN platform compliance checks.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (Commissaire aux comptes) when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds at fiscal year-end: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net revenue excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Mandatory also if the SAS is a consolidating head of a group exceeding the thresholds, controls another entity resulting in group constitution, or if shareholders holding at least 10% of capital or the commercial court request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP as codified in the Plan Comptable Général (ANC Regulation 2014-03, as amended); IFRS is permitted only for consolidated accounts and is not available for the SAS's individual statutory annual accounts.
